Use the Pythagorean identity to find $\cos\theta$, given that $\sin\theta=\dfrac{3}{5}$ and $\theta$ is in the first quadrant.
questions.answer: $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$, so $\cos^2\theta=1-\dfrac{9}{25}=\dfrac{16}{25}$. Since $\theta$ is in the first quadrant, $\cos\theta$ is positive: $\cos\theta=\dfrac{4}{5}$.

questions.q: State the amplitude and period of $y=3\sin(2x)$.
State the amplitude, period, and vertical shift of $y=4\cos(x)+2$.
questions.answer: Amplitude: $4$. Period: $2\pi$ (unchanged, since there is no coefficient on $x$ inside the cosine). Vertical shift: up 2 units.

sections.heading: Applications of trigonometry to real-world problems

questions.q: This question has two parts. A surveyor stands 200 feet from the base of a tower and measures the angle of elevation to the top as $38^\circ$. (a) Find the height of the tower, to the nearest foot. (b) If the surveyor moves 50 feet closer to the tower, find the new angle of elevation, to the nearest degree, using the height found in part (a).
questions.answer: (a) Height $=200\tan(38^\circ)\approx200(0.7813)\approx156$ feet. (b) New distance: $200-50=150$ feet. New angle: $\theta=\arctan\left(\dfrac{156}{150}\right)=\arctan(1.04)\approx46^\circ$.

questions.q: If $\sin\theta=\dfrac{5}{13}$, find $\csc\theta$.

From the top of a 100-foot cliff, the angle of depression to a boat is $25^\circ$. Find the horizontal distance from the base of the cliff to the boat, to the nearest foot.
questions.answer: The angle of depression from the top equals the angle of elevation from the boat. Using the tangent ratio: $\tan(25^\circ)=\dfrac{100}{d}$, so $d=\dfrac{100}{\tan(25^\circ)}\approx\dfrac{100}{0.4663}\approx214$ feet.

sections.heading: Solving trigonometric equations over a restricted domain

questions.q: Solve $2\cos\theta+1=0$ for $0^\circ\leq\theta<360^\circ$.
questions.answer: $\cos\theta=-\dfrac{1}{2}$. Solutions in $[0^\circ,360^\circ)$: $\theta=120^\circ$ or $\theta=240^\circ$ (both quadrants where cosine is negative).
